Reviewed exactly which October column is seasonally adjusted; raw population footnote retained. All published counts converted from thousands to persons; expected rates kept as printed after percent-to-fraction conversion. Labor-force sum checks tolerate only justified rounding, not source sampling error. Independent rosters check numerator populations and zero/upper boundaries. Toolkit validation logs accompany bundle/ZIP; pending scientific review. Duplicate search includes b01-b04, supplied 37-record inventory and runtime snapshot only. Toolkit JSON validation passed: four models, 12 arithmetic references and 11 rejection cases, all requires-extension; final edit revalidated before packing.
handoff.summary: Four CPS status definitions: civilian labor force, unemployment, participation, employment-population ratio. Named rates differ by actual numerator/denominator meaning and are not treated as interchangeable dimensionless ratios. Historical published checks use the 2024-11-01 release vintage with rounding propagation, plus independent synthetic rosters and boundaries. Earlier 15 model IDs remain intact.

assumptions: Source convention: employment and unemployment are disjoint, exhaustive labor-force statuses within the CPS universe.
Application consistency: common reference week, population/subgroup, weights/vintage and adjustment basis; headcounts rather than job counts.

gaps: New CPS person/status meanings and reference-week/vintage/adjustment metadata; persons unit not in runtime snapshot. Midyear_resident_population from b04 is not equivalent to CPS eligible population.

models.inverse_notes: E=LF-U given LF,U and require LF>=U>=0; U=LF-E given LF,E and require LF>=E>=0. No denominators, unique scalar solutions. Roster check LF=11,U=3 recovers E=8; forward LF=11. At LF=0 nonnegative inputs imply E=U=0 uniquely if either is unknown; no ambiguity. If only LF known and both E,U unknown, nonnegative partitions are underdetermined. Rounded national LF inversion may differ from a separately published component within source rounding bounds; no statistical estimation implied.
limitations: Does not classify individuals, estimate sample weights, resolve survey errors or seasonally adjust counts.
Independently rounded published totals may not exactly equal the sum of rounded components; statistical sampling error is separate from arithmetic rounding.

references.method: Published LF 168479 thousand converted to expected 168479000 persons; do not replace with recomputed 168480000. Each input/output is rounded to nearest 1000, so worst-case propagated bound is 500+500+500=1500 persons. This is a rounding consistency test, not an uncertainty interval for survey estimation.
references.provenance: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_11012024.htm, Table A-1 TOTAL, seasonally adjusted October 2024, same archived vintage.

references.method: Independent eligible-population roster: 15 uniquely identified synthetic eligible persons, four outside labor force; enumerating persons not outside yields 11. Disjoint employed roster has eight and unemployed roster three. Checks union count against complementary status count.

references.method: Ideal boundary: no eligible persons classified employed or unemployed yields empty labor-force union, even if some persons remain outside labor force.

rejection_cases.reason: Unemployment count missing; no default zero.

relationship.locator: Civilian labor force subsection; corroborated BLS How Government Measures Unemployment, Basic concepts
relationship.original_equation: Civilian labor force = employed persons + unemployed persons.
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced E,U,LF map source prose counts. Dimensions person+person=person. No percentage scaling or time integration. Mutually exclusive classifications and equal sample weights/coverage are required; duplicated persons would invalidate addition. Survey-weighted estimates can be nonintegers even though persons are individually counted once. The mathematical identity allows E=U=0; a subsequent unemployment rate would then be undefined. Published separately rounded components may miss rounded LF by 1000 persons without contradicting the definition.

sources.evidence: CPS civilian population is age 16+ outside institutions and active-duty armed forces. Mutually exclusive employed/unemployed classifications form labor force. Unemployment divides unemployed by labor force; participation divides labor force by eligible population; employment-population divides employed by eligible population. Counts refer to persons, not jobs.

models.inverse_notes: U=u*LF for 0<=u<=1,LF>0; LF=U/u for u>0,U>0, retaining U<=LF. Check u=.25,LF=12 gives U=3; forward .25. At u=U=0 every LF>0 fits; u=0,U>0 incompatible. U=0,u>0 infers LF=0, excluded. LF is not reconstructed by this inverse when both U and u zero, and no causal labor-supply response is identified.
limitations: Does not estimate survey weights, seasonal adjustment, sampling error or a labor-market behavioral relationship.
Different person denominators define different rates; no substitution between labor force and whole eligible population. Rounding tolerance below is not a survey confidence interval.

references.method: Published 4.1 percent unemployment rate converted to expected fractional 0.041. Counts in source thousands converted to persons. Half of .1 percentage point is .0005 in fraction units; nearest-thousand count rounding adds less than .000004 by (500+ratio*500)/(denominator-500). Bound .000504 propagates both, rather than pretending rounded counts are exact. No statistical uncertainty estimated.
